_comment:
Four bounces of decreasing height - 0.34, 0.21, 0.12, 0.05 - so the arc dies out like a dropped ball instead of stopping dead. That decay IS the comedy: a character too happy to stand still, running out of spring. PURE tier 1-3. The bounce itself is a whole-actor `move.dy` because whole-actor moves TWEEN and that is the only thing that gives air time; the squash and stretch are ad-hoc `parts` transforms on `body`, which SNAP, which is exactly right for a takeoff and a landing. No arms are animated, because arms are not a guaranteed part - the vertical stretch reads as arms-up and costs nothing.

SEMANTIC NOTE: `move.dy` is treated as an offset from the mark the role was bound to, the same as a role `at.dy`, so `dy: 0.0` is the ground. Every bounce lands back at 0.0 and the gag ends on the ground with no scale touched at all.

Deliberately NOT animated: legs, arms, any clip. Nothing here needs a rig to declare anything.
triggers: jumping up and down with excitement

agent._comment: ToonRigRepair guarantees body/head/mouth/eyes on every character rig, so this casts on anything that will ever be made.

beats._comment: the crouch, HELD 0.28s before anything moves. This is the whole gag - a bounce with no anticipation reads as a rendering glitch.
stretch on takeoff. Parts SNAP, so the change from crouch to stretch happens on one frame, which is what sells the pop.
bounce 1, the tallest. Eased whole-actor move = real air time. No `scale` and no `scaleBy` anywhere in this gag, so there is no stage scale to restore.
at the apex the body goes back to rest - an empty transform set restores the rig's own rest pose. Floating in neutral at the top of the arc is what reads as hang time.
landing squash, 0.18s after the move so it is visible at 12fps
a small one, on the biggest landing only. Joy is not an earthquake.
shallower squash - the squash decays with the bounce
bounce 4 - barely off the floor, silent. The one that says the spring is gone.
put down. Back on the mark, body already at rest - the gag leaves nothing behind.
